title: Keep the ticket list working when a row can't be read

blocks.text: This practice continues the ticket store: the starter is the previous practice's solution, with two new methods for the agents' ticket list, `stateLabel` and `countIn`.

The list now meets rows its release can't read. During a rolling deploy, servers running the release after this one already write `ESCALATED` while this release still serves the list, and tickets imported from the old help-desk tool have no state at all. Today one such row makes the whole list fail.

Finish `tryRead` in `src/main/java/practice/TicketStore.java`, which both methods call for every row. When you're done, a row this release can't read shows as `unknown` and is left out of the counts, and every other row, `WAITING` included, reads as before. About six lines in total.

cases.says: rows saved by this release or the previous one, and imported rows with a known state, are labelled and counted
a state name this release doesn't declare reads as unknown, and the other rows are still counted
a row with no state at all reads as unknown instead of failing
a state whose toString() is display text is still read from the text the store wrote

origin.section: valueOf Accepts Only the Exact Name and Throws on Anything Else

concepts: valueOf accepts only the exact name, never returns null, throws IllegalArgumentException on an unknown name and NullPointerException on null, so a reader of stored names decides what an unknown one means.
